title: Provenance-backed prompt snapshot + rollback CI adapter
author: Aisha Banerjee
release_notes: Adds provenance-backed prompt-set snapshotting and a CI adapter that can auto-create snapshots and perform policy-driven rollback on detected regressions. No breaking API changes.
description: Motivation: Flaky regressions in prompt-sets are often hard to trace because we lack a reliable provenance trail for what inputs, seed variants, and annotations produced the baseline metrics. This PR adds a provenance-backed prompt snapshot format (signed manifest + deterministic content hash) and a CI adapter that can both auto-snapshot on prompt-set edits and perform an automated rollback veto when a gated regression is detected. Goals: 1) make prompt-set changes auditable (who changed, original source, transform pipeline, annotation version); 2) make CI decisions repeatable by pinning snapshots with deterministic hashes; 3) provide an operator-friendly rollback path with human-review metadata and replay commands. What this PR does (high level): - Introduces new snapshot manifest schema: provenance fields (origin_url, author, annotation_version, transform_pipeline_id, recorded_seed_map, ingestion_commit) plus signed_manifest (optional). - Adds deterministic content hashing routine (sha256 over canonicalized prompt content + normalized metadata) and a snapshot registry under eval-harness/snapshots/ with index.json that references manifests. - CI adapter: a new Eval CI hook that runs after prompt-set PRs; it will create a snapshot for the changed prompt-set, run the usual regression suite against both the previous snapshot and the candidate snapshot, compute delta metrics, and optionally block the merge if configured SLOs are violated. The adapter emits a compact failure report that includes per-example lineage (prompt id -> snapshot id -> originating file/commit). - Rollback utility: a CLI helper (evalctl snapshot rollback <snapshot-id>) which creates a candidate PR that reverts the prompt-set to a chosen snapshot and attaches an explanation and audit trail. - Backwards compat: existing eval runners can still reference prompt-sets by path; snapshots are optional and only created when the adapter is enabled. Checklist: - [x] manifest schema and serializer/deserializer - [x] canonicalization and deterministic hashing - [x] snapshot registry implementation + index rotator - [x] CI adapter with gating config and retry logic - [x] CLI rollback helper + PR template - [x] unit tests for manifest parsing and hashing - [x] integration smoke test against local runner - [x] docs: brief README and example workflow Usage notes and links: Linear: ENG-4312 (snapshot design), ENG-4320 (ci adapter policy). Related: SUP-1203 incident that motivated per-example lineage. Example workflow: 1) Developer edits prompts in prompts/usability/*.json and opens PR. 2) CI adapter runs, creates snapshot S-2026-02-20-187654 and runs delta evals vs S-2026-02-10-base. 3) If delta breaches configured thresholds the adapter posts a comment with a compact failure report and sets merge status to failure. 4) Author may invoke evalctl snapshot rollback S-2026-02-10-base which creates a revert PR and attaches the signed manifest. Data model notes: snapshot manifest example fields: snapshot_id, created_by, created_at, canonical_hash, origin_commit, input_globs, annotation_version, transform_pipeline_id, recorded_seed_map, signed_manifest_blob (optional). Security and audit: manifests can be signed by the CI runner's key to help with audit; the registry index maintains an append-only log pattern to make retroactive changes visible. Backfill strategy: the adapter will attempt to create snapshots for prompt-sets that change going forward; backfilling older prompt-sets is supported via evalctl snapshot create --from-commit. Testing: added unit tests for hash stability (various whitespace / key-order variants) and an integration scenario that simulates a semantic regression due to an annotation change. See tests/e2e/test_provenance_snapshot.py for the scenario. Caveats and limitations: snapshot creation increases CI runtime by ~10–20% for large prompt-sets; adapter has opt-out by repo/team in .evalconfig; signed manifests require a key provisioning step for private deployments. Implementation notes: commits are intentionally split: first commit implements manifest types and hash util, second commit adds registry and tests, third commit adds CI adapter and rollback CLI. Rollout plan: enable as opt-in on eval-harness and select internal repos for two weeks of dogfooding, then flip opt-in by default for team repos.
